name: Hanun
bio: Hanun was king of the Ammonites, son of Nahash, who succeeded his father on the throne. When David sent envoys to console Hanun and honor his father's memory, Hanun's officials convinced him the men were really spies, so he seized David's envoys, shaved off half of each man's beard, cut their garments off at the hips, and sent them away in humiliation (2 Samuel 10:1-4). Realizing he had made himself an object of hatred to David, Hanun hired thousands of Aramean mercenaries to fight alongside the Ammonites, but Joab and Abishai routed both armies, and the Ammonites shut themselves up in their capital, Rabbah, where the war would continue until its fall two chapters later (2 Samuel 10:5-14; 12:26-31).
